answer: One credential per attested chip: the signing key is fused at manufacture and non-exportable, the issuer dedups chips against their maker-signed certs, and each credential claims at most one capped reward share per epoch. The fuse blocks badge rental, so k identities cost k rented instances, and the share cap sits below that rental: extra keys are strictly loss-making — no cheap multiplier, whatever hardware tide arrives. One chip on a knoll and a rack on a mesa face the same per-instance rule. Leak: caps must track rental prices; maker and cloud are trusted.
